searchText: <Highlander1969> @vb271828 presume you are talking about state trees, right? If so, then one would have to first standardize the definitio(s) of state, it's components,and corresponding state representations first before standardizing on tree structures, no? I am not aware that such standardized definitions, components and representations exist. <vb271828> aren't those definitions part of the EVM? <thegaram33> I don't think it's uniform. Scroll for instance adds 2 new fields (CodeSize and PoseidonCodeHash) to the StateAccount data structure. and, of course, different L2s might use different tree structures, hash functions, etc. (re @vb271828: aren't those definitions part of the EVM?) <vb271828> right but if it makes sense to add these things then surely they can be standardized so we can have one common structure? <vb271828> verkle trees also have a field for code size <thegaram33> it might be possible but I feel like standardization is premature at this point. what's the main benefit that you have in mind? standard state proofs and on-chain state proof verifiers? <vb271828> light clients CCIP verifiers for ENS names ZK proof of state <Highlander1969> Then you need proper definition of e.g. core state and state extensions etc. given the different use cases <vb271828> I'm thinking EVM-specific here <vb271828> if you have extensions then of course that may need custom treatment
